audience.type_b_definition: A Type B reader can reason over this portable packet but cannot inspect or change the live repositories and did not run the checks. Type A/B denotes substrate authority, not intelligence or model quality.
audience.task: Explain, question, compare, or audit the public material from this file; cite record paths; return conclusions as text for a human or Type A agent to carry back.

type_b_orientation.what_the_hell_this_is: Plectis is an open-source mathematics project. Its primary repository, plectis-erdos, carries research on eight still-open Erdős problems: formal source, partial results, explanations, failed routes and contribution tools. The separate plectis repository publishes reusable software components with local checks. This packet carries the published papers and reading material from both repositories. Reading a proof or receipt is not rerunning it.
do_not_confuse: 88 components and 103 paper modules are different inventories: components are runnable/public claim units; paper modules are explanatory subsystem records. They are not one-to-one.
A paper is exposition. Checked Lean source is proof authority; the Lean claims registry owns public claim status; this build ran no Lean kernel.
The doctrine carried here is the complete public doctrine projection, not private raw seed or every internal doctrine record in ai_workflow.
Repository maps are counted, hash-bound depth-two topologies. They avoid embedding thousands of repeated path prefixes; follow public_tree_url for an exact leaf outside the named entrypoints.

headline_results.what_this_is: Work on eight unsolved Erdős problems: #68, #243, #249, #251, #257, #269, #1041, and #1049. All eight remain open; none is solved here. #249 and #257 are the two reviewed core programmes carrying the curated claims registry below; the other six are problem-owned expansion lanes whose per-problem authority is the problems index. What exists is a body of exact reductions, unconditional finite exclusions, structural theorems and machine-checked supporting mathematics, each stated at its own strength -- plus, for #269, a two-prime transcendence result established by a paper argument using Bugeaud-Laurent, deliberately not a Lean theorem, recorded as such in its problem row.

per_problem.question: Is the series sum_{n >= 2} 1/(n! - 1) irrational?
what_is_checked: The exact integral normal form: the series is irrational if and only if the strict factorial successor Z_m misses divisibility by m cofinally.
The equivalent carry form: rationality is equivalent to eventual unit carry, so cofinally many non-unit carries imply irrationality.
Canonical factorial digits, exact remainder recurrences, zero-tail propagation, and the divisor-factorial centre recurrence.
Integral channel congruences, the lcm tax, the prime unit translator, and factorial-grid Cramer residual identities.
Weighted projection and factor-split rigidity consumers with their exact modular and Archimedean hypotheses.
The zero-plateau and first-exit carry dichotomy, prime-power prefix obstructions, and exact doubled-prime branch characterisations.

A Lean-checked implication from one exact non-unit carry to a rational-denominator lower bound; a fresh exact GMP certificate at m = 300000 supplies the finite input used by the papers; the event-trace and unit carries match the previously retained receipt.
what_is_not_checked: Irrationality of the factorial-denominator series.
A theorem producing cofinally many divisibility misses or non-unit carries.
Cofinal strict nonintegrality of the factorial-grid Cramer residual.
The weighted collision-product and complementary-residue estimates needed by the factor-split projection consumer.
The GMP computation is an exact finite external certificate, not a Lean evaluation and not an unbounded argument.

open_obligations.statement: On an unbounded family of tailored prime blocks, prove both the weighted collision-core product bound and the independent complementary-residue inequality consumed by the exact unit-factor scale split.
At infinitely many genuinely nonterminal indices, prove quantitative repeated-support valuation amplification strong enough to meet the checked endpoint inequality.
For infinitely many primes, force the reduced predecessor gap outside the exact lower unit-carry cylinder.
For infinitely many odd primes, rule out both exact p^2-divisibility branches at index 2p by coupling the carry value to the predecessor residue.

Construct an unbounded factorial-grid family whose exact Cramer residual is nonintegral, using a determinant, valuation, cancellation, or gcd-of-minors certificate that controls the finite sign-changing block.

per_problem.question: Under a rapid-growth hypothesis on an integer sequence, does rationality of its reciprocal sum force the sequence to satisfy the Sylvester recurrence eventually?
what_is_checked: The exact product-cleared tail dynamics and the defect identity, as identities in the integer state variables.
That a vanishing centred state is absorbing under strict centring, so the state is either eventually zero or nowhere zero.
That eventual vanishing of the centred state, with the next tail state nonvanishing, forces the Sylvester recurrence eventually.
That a nonnegative centred state vanishes eventually, by descent.
That the centred state cannot be eventually constant and negative, at any magnitude and any common scale.
That the negative magnitude cannot be eventually periodic with positive drift, in the regime where each magnitude is below its multiplier.
A coprimality barrier: a sequence tending to infinity with uniformly bounded upward increments cannot permanently avoid infinitely many fresh pairwise coprime moduli.
That a reduced exact tail has pairwise coprime multipliers which its numerator permanently avoids, so no such tail has a divergent numerator with bounded rise.
That the tail gcd stabilises under cofinally bounded negative magnitudes.
Conditionally: exact dynamics, eventual strict centring, an eventually bounded negative part, and normalised vanishing together force the centred state to vanish eventually.
That survival through a fixed number of forced updates depends only on the initial state modulo a factorial of the horizon.
what_is_not_checked: The unrestricted problem.

That eventual strict centring and normalised vanishing follow from the growth hypothesis and rationality. Both are assumed by the final theorem and neither is derived, so that theorem constrains the state system rather than the original sequence.
Any exclusion of negative excursions whose magnitudes are unbounded along a cofinal set.
The criterion of Erdos and Straus and Duverney's conditional characterisation, which are cited rather than formalised and are both stronger than anything checked here.

open_obligations.statement: Exclude, or construct, an exact orbit whose centred state is negative infinitely often with magnitudes unbounded along that cofinal set. Every checked exclusion consumes some finiteness: a fixed set of prime divisors, a fixed period, or a fixed bound on the negative part.
Derive eventual strict centring and normalised vanishing from the growth hypothesis and rationality, or show that they do not follow.
Kernel-check the Erdos-Straus weighted criterion and Duverney's conditional characterisation under explicit analytic hypotheses.

per_problem.question: Is the dyadic series sum p_n/2^n over consecutive primes irrational? Equivalently, is the corresponding consecutive-prime-gap dyadic series irrational?
what_is_checked: The finite summation-by-parts identity relating the prime dyadic partial sums to the prime-gap dyadic partial sums, with an exact endpoint term and no convergence premise.
The factor-of-two normalisation between the two displayed indexings, at every finite horizon.
Conditional on summability of the prime dyadic series, the exact infinite prime-gap identity and the equivalence of irrationality of the prime and prime-gap series.
For an abstract integer-digit dyadic tail recurrence: the exact block identity, and that a shift of fixed length is integral exactly when an explicit scaled state is.
That one integral shift propagates to every later index.
That repeated doubling removes the power-of-two denominator, so every rational-valued dyadic recurrence has one fixed positive shift integral at all sufficiently late indices.
For a real-valued dyadic recurrence, cofinal non-integrality of every fixed positive shift implies irrationality of the initial state.
That the actual consecutive-prime-gap sequence is unbounded, by the factorial prime-free-interval construction, and therefore is not eventually periodic with any positive period.
For any integer-digit dyadic tail recurrence, two adjacent fixed-length shifts lying strictly between -1 and 1 cannot both be integral when the corresponding digits differ.
For the actual prime gaps, a cofinal supply of adjacent small-shift pairs with a mismatching gap excludes eventual integrality of that fixed shift.
The generic distance-to-integers core of the finite-truncation criterion: an approximation farther than its error bound from every integer certifies non-integrality.
what_is_not_checked: The target irrationality.

The definition and recurrence of the concrete prime-gap tail as Lean infinite sums; the note supplies these at paper level. Summability of the concrete prime series is Lean-checked unconditionally via an elementary polynomial prime bound.
A theorem supplying cofinally many adjacent actual-prime-gap tail shifts in the open unit interval with the required gap mismatch.
Any theorem forcing periodicity or automaticity of the prime gaps from rationality; the free-carry identity disconfirms that route.

open_obligations.statement: For every fixed h >= 1 and every N0, find N >= N0 for which sum_{j>=1} (g_{N+h+j}-g_{N+j})/2^j is not an integer.

For every fixed h >= 1 and every N0, find N >= N0 such that both adjacent full tail shifts have absolute value less than 1 and g_{N+h+1} != g_{N+1}. The checked local consumer then excludes eventual integrality of the h-shift.

Formalise summability of the actual prime and prime-gap dyadic series and identify the concrete infinite prime-gap tail with the checked real/rational dyadic recurrence, so the local consumer reaches the target series without a paper-only analytic bridge.

what_is_checked: That for three pairwise distinct primes the least common multiple of the smooth prefix equals the product of the three maximal pure prime powers below the cutoff.
That equal logarithmic coordinates give an equal prefix least common multiple, so the running value is constant on logarithmic cells.
That advancing exactly one logarithmic coordinate multiplies the running value by the corresponding prime.
That the positive power channels of distinct primes are disjoint, so the first powers in three channels give an exact jump count.
That a finite smooth lattice sum groups exactly by running height, with the height fibre cardinality as coefficient.
A quadratic bound on the cardinality of the actual filtered exponent shell.

That each dyadic block contains at most one internal pure power from each non-dyadic channel, so the compressed {2,3,5} block radix belongs to the exact alphabet {2,6,10,30} and in particular lies between 2 and 30.
That the smallest {2,3,5} kernel rectangle has determinant exactly -1/15, so its two-by-two matrix has rank two over the rationals and no rank-one separation exists.
The canonical least-positive-residue interval and congruence facts, including the zero-residue representative.
The exact local-window identity for an integral carry.
A denominator-dependent CofinalLocalWindowEscape proposition and the full theorem that it rules out every positive reduced integral carry satisfying the matching bound.
A bounded-radix dichotomy: under a bounded positive digit alphabet, a nonzero scaled tail must be separated from the integers cofinally.
Exact three-channel block-nullity as a coboundary condition, and extinction of a bounded carry lift under two independent anchors.
The exact residue-digit plus coboundary form of an integral carry, together with a function-faithful observer criterion and a finite realised-span consequence.

The derivation of the actual bounded positive carry, including the divisibility required to cancel the absorbed smooth denominator factor, from a hypothetical rational value of the original series.
CofinalLocalWindowEscape for those actual words; it is an explicit hypothesis of the checked consumer, not a theorem.
A proof that the actual three-channel word satisfies the block-null, anchor, or factorisation hypotheses of the migrated abstract consumers.
The infinite limit of the jump expansion; only its finite core is checked.
Any unbounded denominator exclusion. The finite certificates exclude denominators below an explicit bound and no further.

per_problem.question: For a monic polynomial whose roots lie in the open unit disc, must two roots be joinable by a curve of length less than two inside the open unit lemniscate?
what_is_checked: Along a trajectory tangent to the complex Newton vector field -f/f', the polynomial value satisfies w' = -w.
The exponentially rescaled polynomial value is a first integral, so the value of a Newton trajectory remains on one oriented ray.
A finite Newton-flow connection can only join endpoints whose polynomial values lie on the same positive ray; distinct critical-value arguments therefore exclude such a connection.
For two translated critical values, the ray-collision locus is a real affine line with an exact one-parameter description.
A finite family of ray-collision lines can be avoided by an arbitrarily small common translation.
An explicit root-retention estimate keeps roots of a sufficiently small constant perturbation inside the unit disc.
what_is_not_checked: Erdos Problem 1041 in unrestricted degree.

The spanning-tree decomposition claimed in the March 2026 manuscript; its printed Proposition 12 proof uses an invalid three-ended local saddle block, and a Cassini example refutes the printed global tree budget.
A repair of Proposition 12 that retains the printed 1/(2π) spanning-tree coefficient; any later argument must change the metric inequality.
A perturbation theorem that first makes critical values injective while preserving the relevant lemniscate component, collars, and strict length slack.
The global planar decomposition and metric gluing needed to obtain a curve of length less than two.

open_obligations.statement: The printed 1/(2π) spanning-tree estimate of Proposition 12 is false. Any later argument must pay a positive attachment cost, select only one short pair, or use a different global metric inequality.
Build a compact strip or cell decomposition after cutting along critical-value rays, without presupposing the unproved local valence count.
Glue the local pieces with strict quantitative slack while preserving the sharp one-over-two-pi length bookkeeping.
First separate critical values, then apply the checked small translation, while retaining roots, the selected component, collars, ray separation, and a strict length margin.
Prove the global relative Newton-flow theorem that turns the checked ray separation into the required root-to-root curve inside the original open lemniscate.

per_problem.question: For which rational bases is the corresponding series irrational? The first resistant explicit base is three halves.
what_is_checked: That a literal coordinatewise transfer of the integer-base clearing argument forces a power-versus-linear inequality, and that this inequality is impossible at base three halves.
The exact denominator-cleared rational-base tail recurrence, including its forcing term.
That for every noninteger base with denominator at least two the forcing magnitude grows at least exponentially, while at denominator one it collapses to a bounded expression.
The complete elementary Archimedean height inequality used by the published Bundschuh-Väänänen criterion at base seven halves; the analytic irrationality theorem itself remains external.
Polynomial bounds on the doubled denominator exponents in the homogenised Padé construction, together with an exact gap identity.
The exact exterior-determinant elimination identity, and that rowwise contents scale the Padé errors, exterior determinant, and absolute determinant height by the same factors.
The exact Heine-Zudilin cone endpoint exponent arithmetic used to identify the bottom and top coefficient endpoints.
That homogeneous evaluation at (3,2) sees only the constant endpoint modulo three and the top endpoint modulo two, so unit endpoints obstruct common local factors.

That under unit top and constant endpoint hypotheses, a common multiplier of the two specialised coefficient channels is divisible by neither two nor three; the missing local gain must therefore survive primitive normalisation.
That vanishing of the higher bottom and top endpoint jets is exactly divisibility by the corresponding powers of three and two.
That the source integer-base ratio inequality implies a strictly negative scalar product-formula margin at three halves.

That the four-jet target has exact cardinality (3^R)^2(2^S)^2 and, for positive R, any family with n at least 4R+2S forces two distinct binary selectors to collide; their {-1,0,1} difference cancels all four endpoint jets.
That the rectangular Hermite-Pade threshold never improves on the classical one in the checked exponent model, with equality characterised exactly.
The exact 81/200 height region: 31/4 and every positive power lie inside it and outside the earlier Bundschuh-Vaananen region, while 3/2 lies outside both.

At n = 0, the Amdeberhan-Zeilberger q-Apery operator applied to Van Assche's moving diagonal has residual -p(p-1)^2(p+1)(p^5+2p^4+2p^3+2p^2+2), which is strictly negative and nonzero for every real p > 1.
what_is_not_checked: The universal rational-base conjecture, including the case 3/2, remains open. The checked 31/4 power family settles one region and leaves that conjecture untouched.
The published analytic height theorem, which is cited and used as an external result and is not formalised here.
The all-scale Heine-Zudilin coefficient construction at rational base three halves; the primary source assumes an integer base.
The source analytic irrationality theorem inside the 81/200 height region; only its elementary parameter specialisations are formalised.
A sufficiently large primitive-normalised, non-collapsed coefficient family meeting the checked n >= 4R+2S threshold at the required quadratic depths.
That one of the resulting bounded-coefficient collision vectors has a nonzero polynomial pair, lies outside the analytic remainder nullspace, and has sufficient local gain.
Positivity or decay of the elementary Padé remainder; only its exponent arithmetic is checked.

Any general recurrence, endpoint, lattice, valuation, denominator, or irrationality conclusion from the n = 0 q-Apery residual; it proves only that the named scalar recurrence does not transfer to Van Assche's diagonal.

open_obligations.statement: After dividing every coefficient pair by its rowwise common content, at positive quadratic target depths R_n,S_n exhibit at least 4R_n+2S_n primitive coefficient pairs from a genuinely non-collapsed deformation, prove that the required two-adic and three-adic gain survives primitive normalisation, and prove that at least one resulting checked {-1,0,1} collision has a nonzero polynomial pair and lies outside the analytic remainder nullspace; or prove an exact rank obstruction.

headline_results.status_counts_reading: These are registry statuses, not quality grades. 'proved here' means a Lean proof term is accepted for that statement; 'conditional reduction' means an exact equivalence whose two sides may both remain open; 'unconditional progress' means an unconditional theorem about the open problem itself.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Unbounded and non-eventually-periodic consecutive prime gaps
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: The consecutive-prime-gap sequence is unbounded and is not eventually periodic with any positive period. These coefficient facts do not by themselves imply irrationality of the prime-gap or prime-index dyadic series.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Finite Newton-flow ray separation and perturbation consumer
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: An explicit exponential-decay Newton connection can occur only when its endpoint values lie on the same positive ray; conversely, every finite injective complex family admits an arbitrarily small common translation making all values nonzero and all positive-ray arguments distinct. These are finite perturbative and conditional connection statements.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Quotient-band channel breakpoint for factorial moments
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For a finite integer coefficient family whose indices all lie in one quotient band k·d ≤ i_j < (k+1)·d, the factorial moment is exactly (d!)^k times the d-channel numerator. In the first band d ≤ i_j < 2d, channel cancellation forces the factorial moment to vanish; with all indices at least d and a nonzero moment, some index is therefore at least 2d.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Finite least-positive-residue contradiction for #269
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For a positive modulus C, a positive integer state c bounded by K cannot be congruent to x modulo C when the canonical least-positive representative of x is greater than K; the zero residue class is represented by C. The integer carry form and exact residue classifier are checked in Lean.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Finite #269 radix prefixes admit an altered rational completion
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: Every finite positive integral radix prefix with nonnegative integral digits extends to a positive rational orbit by changing the future to radix 2 and digit 1. In particular, the actual word through any finite horizon has such an abstract completion. This is a countermodel to finite-prefix-only inference and is not a rational model of the actual infinite smooth-number series.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Size-authenticated bounded certificate checks for #269
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: The bounded width and cumulative-array checkers expose their size hypotheses, are sound on every accessed entry, compose across adjacent ranges, and carry explicit regressions showing that default-zero array access, half-height cancellation, and finite coverage cannot certify an infinite/cofinal conclusion. No paper numerical table is executed or validated by these safety theorems alone.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Canonical quotient-greedy and scaled-remainder frontier at 1/21
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: Membership of 1/21 in the Mersenne achievement set is equivalent both to excluding one explicit fatal/cofinite/aligned branch and to cofinally bounded scaled actual greedy remainders. Every closed Boolean quotient row is the deterministic quotient-greedy row; any unbounded sequence of canonical rows with remainder at most 2^R gives membership. On the complementary fatal branch the remainder is eventually strictly supercapacity, the boundary rank is always selected, and support and remainder follow one exact affine recurrence. A final skipped exponent also forces a structured one-sided approximation to the Erdős–Borwein constant with exact denominator-order constraints. These results isolate permanent affine supercapacity as the surviving late regime; they do not contradict it or prove 1/21 membership.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Explicit basis of the dyadic totient kernel span
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: Lean constructs an explicit odd-core-indexed basis of the rational span of the full dyadic totient kernel, with exact span equality and linear independence. This is an independent constructive proof route; its infinite-dimensionality consequence is not an independent contribution because Coons's non-2-regularity theorem already implies it.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Dyadic totient-kernel finite-level rank
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every e, a CRT–Dirichlet construction produces a separated nonzero evaluation minor for the canonical dyadic totient-kernel family, which is linearly independent with exact span dimension 2^e + 1. The same Lean development proves that the full dyadic kernel span is not finite-dimensional, but that corollary is not an independent contribution: it is equivalent, for this integer-valued sequence module, to Coons's non-2-regularity theorem. Even residues reduce to odd-core channels, and the compressed-adjoint boundary remains available. These coefficient-side theorems do not prove that S is irrational.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Campbell shift-synchronization strategy boundary
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: Campbell's application of the Alford-Granville-Pomerance estimate chooses delta = 1/4, so at prime-search height X the progression modulus d must satisfy d <= X^(1/4), equivalently d^4 <= X. In the proposed last-skip synchronization, P is the fatal-window prime cap, t the unavoidable phase period, and d the combined progression modulus. Taking X = P, the requirements 2 <= d, t <= d, P <= 4t, and d^4 <= P are inconsistent. The shifted-zero interface is guarded by a putative last skip and is exactly equivalent to infinitely many actual greedy skips and to membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set. It is an endpoint restatement, not an independent Campbell input, and proves no half-membership.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Fixed-precision valuation-unit no-go theorem
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: At every fixed positive precision, every finite word of odd valuation-unit symbols admits a compatible carry orbit from an arbitrary incoming integer state, with each successive state within the corresponding valuation-unit radius. Thus bounded local signatures alone cannot exclude all finite centred endpoints; growing precision or global information remains necessary for an endpoint argument.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: LCM factor-ideal anchor-pulse no-go theorem
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every t ≥ 3, a nonzero synthetic affine carry has forcing letters in the principal ideal generated by φ(lcm(1,…,t)), matches every stated whole-ray anchor, and remains within the diagonal bounds while its state is a strict survivor. The same countermodel survives every finite integer shift polynomial. Thus factor ideals, whole-ray anchors, and finite-rank shift algebra alone do not force carry escape. The construction does not assert that its forcing letters are actual totient differences and does not rule out nonlinear use of fresh divisor channels.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Actual LCM positive corridor and top-edge boundary
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For a ≥ 8 and J + (a + 6) < 2·2^a, the true translated LCM-orbit difference is strictly positive. If it is represented by an integer and the dyadic modulus has room for the directed endpoint strip, the carry survivor is strictly negative and the discrepancy residue is exactly the top-edge representative 2^K − carry_K, strictly between the strip’s lower edge and 2^K. Thus the positive corridor eliminates the nonnegative true survivor but does not itself produce a central-band contradiction; an independent arithmetic exclusion of the top boundary is still required.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Base 3/2 coordinatewise corridor exclusion
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: With N ≥ 1 and K ≥ 1, the six-condition CoordinatewiseCorridor at base 3/2 is impossible for every natural Q and digit. This excludes only that literal coordinatewise clearing architecture, not rationality or irrationality of F(3/2) or any other proof architecture.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Exact rational-base cleared-tail recurrence
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For rational r, s, B, and F, a coefficient sequence coeff : ℕ → ℚ, and r ≠ 0, the denominator-cleared tail state satisfies rationalBaseClearedTailQ (r, s, B, F, coeff) (N + 1) = r · rationalBaseClearedTailQ (r, s, B, F, coeff) N − B · coeff (N + 1) · s^(N + 1) for every N. The identity is not derived from rationality and is not itself a rationality contradiction.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Rational-base forcing-term growth boundary
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For natural s, B, coeff, and N, if s ≥ 2, B ≥ 1, and coeff(N + 1) ≥ 1, then rationalBaseForcingNat s B coeff N ≥ 2^(N + 1); at s = 1 the same quantity is exactly B · coeff(N + 1). This is an elementary forcing-term bound, not a bounded-state contradiction or endpoint result.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Van Assche q-Apéry diagonal recurrence non-transfer
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every real p > 1, the n = 0 residual obtained by applying the Amdeberhan–Zeilberger q-Apéry operator to Van Assche's moving diagonal is the displayed strictly negative factorisation, hence is nonzero. This rules out that selected diagonal for that recurrence at n = 0; it proves no general recurrence, endpoint, or #1049 irrationality result.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Bounded-rise fresh-modulus coprimality barrier
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For natural sequences u and m, if u tends to infinity with upward increments bounded by a fixed positive B, the moduli m are eventually greater than 1 and pairwise coprime, and each earlier m(i) is coprime to every later u(t), then the hypotheses are inconsistent. This is a reusable state-level obstruction, not a proof of the full Erdős #243 assertion.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Eventually-periodic negative-orbit exclusion
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For natural sequences a, D, C, and e with 2 ≤ a(n), positive e(N+n) < a(N+n), the exact recurrences D(n+1) = a(n)·D(n) and C(n+1) = C(n) + e(n), the shape equation D(n) + e(n) = (a(n)−1)·C(n), and a positive-period, positive-drift tail e(N+n+h) = e(N+n) and C(N+n+h) = C(N+n) + M with h > 0 and M > 0, the hypotheses are inconsistent. This is only the eventually-periodic negative-magnitude obstruction; mixed-sign and unbounded-negative behaviour remain outside the claim and the full Erdős #243 endpoint remains open.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Phase-specific density obstruction for the two cubic survivor profiles
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For either surviving cubic profile Q_{12,c}(n)=2n(n+1)(n+2)+c with c=1 or c=-1, the exact tail recurrences force a mismatch in every sufficiently late four-index window at the corresponding phase modulo 7. The mismatch set therefore has lower density at least 1/7, and hence at least the 1/28 stated in the long paper. No phase-free or arbitrary-profile density statement is claimed.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Finite-support denominator period noncollapse
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every finite nonempty support F with 0 ∉ F and integer base b ≥ 2, the reduced denominator of the literal finite sum ∑_{n∈F} 1/(bⁿ−1) is coprime to b and the multiplicative order of b modulo that denominator equals F.lcm id. This finite-support theorem supplies no unbounded support certificate and does not settle the universal infinite-support Erdős #257 endpoint.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Weighted-phase carry split and finite realised span for #269
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: The exact weighted-phase carry recurrence splits into a finite residue digit, each of the two coordinates staying inside its declared interval, and an integral quotient coboundary that is not controlled. An explicit factorisation through a finite-dimensional function-faithful observer then forces the realised symbolic span to be finite. Nothing here proves a finite-state quotient or a literal infinite realised span, and no rationality or irrationality conclusion follows.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Exact finite arithmetic and run-threshold checks for #249
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: The four displayed discrepancy values at (h,X,L)=(1,4,9), their finite room and certified kills, the Farey denominator bound, and the corrected finite run threshold hold exactly. These finite facts do not supply a cofinal certificate producer.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Generic centering countermodel for the #249 decomposition
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: A two-point complex model has vanishing peripheral mean contributions while its centered contribution remains nonzero. This refutes the generic inference from peripheral cancellation to a centered budget; it is not a counterexample to the arithmetic totient-centered predicate.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: One unconditional finite first-harmonic gap instance
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: At (h,X,L)=(1,4,9), the exact finite first-harmonic expression has the certified norm gap bounded by 21X/25. This is one finite instance and does not establish DTWFirstHarmonicNormGap or any cofinal statement.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Full-support Erdős–Borwein irrationality, every integer base b ≥ 2
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every integer b ≥ 2, the series ∑_{n≥1} 1/(bⁿ − 1) is irrational (Erdős, 1948).

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: The Erdős–Borwein constant E is irrational
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: E = ∑_{n≥1} 1/(2ⁿ − 1) is irrational, as the base-2 corollary of the full-support theorem.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Named infinite-support irrationality families toward #257
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every base b ≥ 2, ∑_{n∈A} 1/(bⁿ − 1) is irrational for factorial support, power-of-two support, multiples, pairwise-coprime supports with summable reciprocals, eventually-periodic supports, residue classes, and the odd numbers. Proved families, not the universal statement.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Unconditional denominator exclusion for the totient constant
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: S = ∑ φ(n)/2ⁿ is not equal to p/q for any integer p and any 1 ≤ q ≤ 79 639 646 646 701 375 323 355 774 875 831 053 (≈ 7.96 × 10³⁴). A lower bound on any rational representation, not a proof of irrationality.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Exact reduction of #249 to finite decidable certificates
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: S is irrational if and only if certified non-integrality witnesses occur at unbounded parameters. The pointwise completeness theorem and the diagonal supply theorem together show that an unbounded lcm-diagonal supply is equivalent as well. Producing that supply remains open.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Certificate completeness
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: At fixed parameters, a certified kill exists exactly when the corresponding tail difference is non-integral. At every positive shift, integrality of one tail difference forces S to be rational; thus irrationality is equivalent to pointwise non-integrality, and to pointwise finite certificates.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Initial certified-kill segment and generated certificates
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: Kernel-checked certified kills for the listed small periods, every lcm-diagonal scale t ≤ 82, and the finite certificate shards. The historical 28 explicit deposits through t = 64 form a strict subset of this contiguous finite band.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Exact full-target reduction on the lcm diagonal
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: At each lcm-diagonal scale, integrality is equivalent to a foreign-defect term landing in an explicit full-target interval. Globally, S is irrational if and only if the full target is avoided at arbitrarily large diagonal scales; that cofinal avoidance is not proved.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Scalar-localisation height obstruction
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: If H divides the reduced denominator of a rational x and the reduced denominator of c·x divides H for an integer c, then the complementary factor x.den/H divides |c|. Scalar localisation transfers, rather than discards, that denominator information; this local obstruction is not an irrationality criterion.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: All-base totient-kernel reduction, spanning, and conditional rank
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: For every integer base k at least 2, Lean checks the zero-residue scaling identity, the exact nonzero scalar used in composite-base residue reduction, unique quotient/nonzero-digit coordinates, and cardinality k^e + 1 of the canonical finite-level index. It proves unconditionally that this canonical family spans the complete kernel through level e, and proves exact rank k^e + 1 under the explicit hypothesis that the family is linearly independent. Lean does not prove that hypothesis here; the note's evaluation-matrix argument and AllBaseTotientKernel.lean at public checkpoint 25ef6245d15a discharge it by an independent finite-determinant construction, so the unconditional basis and rank theorem takes Martin's positive-density theorem as prior art rather than as an input.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Sublogarithmic divisor-coverage zero windows
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: A rational support-series value forces every zero window in the divisor-count coefficient to have length at most ε·log₂(N+1) + B, where B ≥ 0 is built from ε, c and v but is bound after the support and numerator, so no single constant is claimed uniform across supports. This constrains coverage; it does not solve universal #257.

bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.label: Greedy geometry of the Mersenne achievement set
bears_directly_on_the_open_problems.statement: The Mersenne achievement set is compact, perfect, totally disconnected, nowhere dense, and has Lebesgue measure one. Membership is equivalent to greedy survival at every level; for the target 1/2 it is exactly equivalent to the canonical greedy orbit omitting infinitely many exponents. No finite normalized support has value 1/2, so positive membership would automatically produce an infinite rational-valued support and refute universal #257. Finite exact-rational death certificates soundly prove non-membership (3/4 is excluded at level one). The strict-tail Cantor geometry is recorded by Kovač–Tao; no novelty claim is made for the formalised refinements.

remaining_open_propositions.statement: Prove that S = ∑_{n≥2} 1/(n! − 1) is irrational.
Prove that S = ∑ φ(n)/2ⁿ is irrational, with no bound on a possible rational denominator.
Prove that Π = ∑_{n≥1} p_n/2ⁿ is irrational; the exact tail-shift equivalence and prime-gap constraints do not supply the required cofinal escape.
Produce certified non-integrality witnesses at unbounded parameters. A sufficient one-parameter form is to produce them along the lcm diagonal.
Decide whether 1/2 lies in the Mersenne achievement set. Yes refutes universal #257; no closes only this route.

Decide the exact 1/21 branch: equivalently, exclude the fatal/cofinite/aligned branch, contradict its eventual permanent affine-supercapacity recurrence, prove cofinally bounded scaled greedy remainders, or force an unbounded sequence of closed canonical quotient rows. A positive membership result would refute universal #257; no such producer is proved.
Prove irrationality for every infinite support A, not only the named support families formalised here.

Determine irrationality of the running-LCM reciprocal sum for finite prime sets of size at least three. For {2,3,5}, the rationality-to-carry bridge is established and cofinal local-window escape remains open.
Find or refute the required short curve between two roots inside the open lemniscate; finite ray separation and perturbative root retention do not supply the global topology and length argument.

Determine whether F(t) = ∑_{n≥1} 1/(tⁿ − 1) is irrational for every rational t > 1. F(31/4) is an ordinary Zudilin specialization, not a Lean theorem; the 3/2 approximant with remainder control and the universal assertion remain open.

Prove the Erdős #243 assertion: if 1 ≤ a₁ < a₂ < ··· has aₙ/aₙ₋₁² → 1 and rational reciprocal sum, then aₙ = aₙ₋₁² − aₙ₋₁ + 1 eventually; the checked barrier does not settle the mixed-sign unbounded regime.
Prove that B·T_a ∉ ℤ for every B ≥ 1 coprime to 30 and every a ≥ 1.
Prove that for every B ≥ 1 coprime to 30 and every a₀ ≥ 1 there are ℓ ≥ a₀ and h ≥ 1 with lpr_{W(ℓ,h)}(−B·F(ℓ,h)) > K(B, ℓ+h), where K is the defined long-paper cap.

Represent D_{2,3,5} faithfully by a specified two-dimensional Mahler-type value theorem with every hypothesis verified, give a conditional theorem under explicit logarithmic nondegeneracy, or prove no such representation exists.
Decide whether every nonterminal canonical orbit of the reduced-orbit problem has limsup_n (log M_n)/n > 0, equivalently 2^n ≤ M_n^K infinitely often for some K ≥ 1.
Decide whether, for each h ≥ 1, some s ≥ 1 and 0 < η < 1 give, for every X₀, admissible X and L meeting the displayed size conditions for which the four first-harmonic bounds hold.
Decide whether the scaled actual greedy remainder returns cofinally to one bounded interval: whether some B < ∞ has 2^N r_N ≤ B at arbitrarily large N.
Decide whether a bounded-memory 2-adic or discrepancy invariant of the actual support forces a closed return or forbids permanent supercapacity, or prove no such invariant exists.
Decide whether the final-skip signatures prove |E − a_M| ≥ gap_M, contradicting 0 < a_M − E < gap_M, for E = ∑_{n≥1}(2^n − 1)^{−1} and the last-skip approximant a_M.

headline_results.how_to_read_this: Each statement is quoted at exactly the strength the registry asserts, including its own negative clause. Do not add a hedge that the statement does not contain, and do not drop one that it does. If you conclude from this packet that the mathematics is thin or unverifiable, name which of these statements you checked and found wanting -- a general impression formed without opening one is not a finding about the work.
headline_results.verification_boundary: No Lean kernel ran during this build. These are registry statuses and source coordinates, so a reader can locate and check each proof; that is a route to verification, not verification itself.

dedupe_strategy.principle: every visible-text body is carried exactly once
dedupe_strategy.pages: prose pages carry full text; the all-components / paper-modules / doctrine / rules / reference-index pages, the per-area pages, and the glossary carry a lede plus content_refs into the atoms (no re-render)
dropped_duplication: the top-level glossary copy (kept once in public_glossary)
paper-module section excerpts (duplicate body_markdown; section_titles kept as a thin TOC)
the component_digest thin projection (full records are in components[])
evidence_profiles[] bodies (already carried by content-graph.json; resolve via evidence_profiles_ref)
rules_and_ideas[] relation rows (already carried by content-graph.json; resolve via rules_and_ideas_ref)

doctrine canonical_body.sections fields that were byte-identical to a top-level field on the same record (the relationships / provenance / statement echo); each record names what was dropped in canonical_body_echo_dropped
dedupe_strategy.relation_layer: paper_module grouped_relation_feeds keep local wiring; the complete relation lattice is referenced through rules_and_ideas_ref
dedupe_strategy.to_go_leaner: thin paper-module grouped relation feeds if needed; bodies are never dropped

Mathematics and research software

### Plectis

Research with AI, mathematics and software.

Plectis publishes mathematics and research software so others can inspect the work and continue it: a Lean repository of research on eight open Erdős problems, a public software toolkit of selected mechanisms from a private research system, and the papers that explain both.

Built and maintained by [Will Cook](index.html#contact). Plectis is independent and self-funded.

[Read the one-page introduction](docs/introduction.html) [PDF](assets/plectis-one-page.pdf) [Explore the mathematics](maths/index.html) [See the maths map](maths/universe.html) [Try the software](docs/quickstart.html) [Lean repository on GitHub](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos) [Plectis repository on GitHub](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis)

Mathematics

#### Eight open Erdős problems.

Each page gives the original question, the results checked in Lean, the approaches that failed and what remains unproved. All eight original problems remain open.

Erdős #68 Open ** [The factorial - denominator series](maths/problems/erdos_68.html)** Erdős #243 Open ** [Reciprocal -tail rigidity near the Sylvester recurrence](maths/problems/erdos_243.html)** Erdős #249 Open ** [The binary totient series](maths/problems/erdos_249.html)** Erdős #251 Open ** [The prime -gap dyadic series](maths/problems/erdos_251.html)** Erdős #257 Open ** [Reciprocal sums over infinite exponent supports](maths/problems/erdos_257.html)** Erdős #269 Open ** [Three- prime running least common multiples](maths/problems/erdos_269.html)** Erdős #1041 Open ** [Short connections inside polynomial lemniscates](maths/problems/erdos_1041.html)** Erdős #1049 Open ** [Lambert-type series at rational bases](maths/problems/erdos_1049.html)**

[Browse the problems and their papers →](maths/index.html) · [Lean repository on GitHub](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos)

Papers

#### Three papers explain the project.

Read any of them online, or open the PDF.

21-page paper ** [Open- source idea paper](maths/papers/open-source-mathematics-strategy.html)** The shared research resource, how people contribute, and how credit is recorded. _From Spare Compute to Cumulative Mathematics_. [PDF](https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/open-source-mathematics-strategy.pdf) 20-page paper ** [Lean system paper](maths/papers/claim-faithful-publication-systems.html)** How finding a result, checking it and deciding what may be claimed stay separate. _Problem-Sized Lean Worlds_. [PDF](https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/claim-faithful-publication-systems-paper.pdf) 22-page paper ** [Software repo paper](maths/papers/plectis-public-system.html)** What the public tests show, who chose them, and what stays unsupported. _Plectis: What a Stranger Can Check_. [PDF](https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/plectis-public-system.pdf)

[Browse all twenty papers, with abstracts and sources →](docs/papers.html)

These are author-released manuscripts. Lean checks the formal statements; novelty and significance need separate assessment against earlier work.

Further reading

#### The principles, the open questions and the two maps.
- [Principles and working rules](docs/doctrine.html)
- [Open questions about AI systems](docs/open-questions.html)
- [Mathematics map](maths/universe.html)
- [Software map](docs/architecture.html#whole-system-map)

Why

#### Why I am building it.

I was vibe-mathing back in early 2025, and even then I immediately realised formal verification is necessary but not sufficient for a lay person wanting to use AI to do maths. The case that AI would eventually be able to do mathematics as well as any human in this decade was strong enough that I decided to try. Trying lets you encounter failure modes, and time spent with them lets you try to fix them. If AI is any level more intelligent than a person, I see no reason why that intelligence can't then be applied to convert the resulting “ uninterpretable ” mathematics back into something that can be interpreted.

I realised I was a good guinea pig, because my mathematics background is so weak that I was a microcosm of what may happen in the next ten years for even experts. I built a larger system with a whole frontend, but I don't want to overload anyone. My hope is the maths will speak for itself, and people can enter that whole rabbit hole after I've passed the credibility bar. There is a lot more than I have covered here.

[The longer account: how this started and what I am trying to do.](docs/contact.html#who-built-this)

Recordings

#### Inside the research system.

The same walkthrough at three lengths: one minute, five minutes and half an hour. They show the private interface; they do not install it or validate it.
1. [1:25](https://youtu.be/R_--vExxWyk)

01 One minute · 1:25

##### The one-minute version

[Watch on YouTube](https://youtu.be/R_--vExxWyk)

The argument in four steps
1. I built a large Python system, with agents helping me build and inspect it. It has more moving parts than I can hold in my head, and more than any agent can hold in its context window.
2. Building got easier faster than understanding what had been built. So the priority became inspection.
3. An agent saying "I committed the fix" doesn't mean much on its own. Agents can lie, or misunderstand, or forget. So a word like "landed" gets read by a mechanical check that runs a real checklist before it counts.
4. My front end could be completely made up and you wouldn't know. The open repo is the part you can actually check.

Read the transcript

I built a large Python system with agents helping me build and inspect it. It now has far more moving parts than I can keep in my head at any one moment, and more than any agent can keep in its context window at any one moment. And building got easier before being able to understand what has been built could catch up.

So it exists because an agent saying "I committed the fix" is pretty ephemeral and doesn't really mean anything. Agents can lie, or agents can misunderstand, or they can forget.

So we essentially have this mechanical, semantic process which is able to actually read the claim. Let's say it says "landed", which is a common word that they use. There's an actual checklist that it has to run in order to make sure that it really is landed.

My entire front end could be completely made up and you wouldn't know. Plectis, the open- source repo, is falsifiable. You can check it. You can really check it.

So I made the public bit as open and clear as I could, but I also needed to be able to signal the capability of the wider system beyond just claiming it.
2. [4:57](https://youtu.be/VoWByIOIuBE)

02 Five minutes · 4:57

##### The five-minute walk-through

[Watch on YouTube](https://youtu.be/VoWByIOIuBE)

The argument in eight steps
1. The system has more moving parts than I can hold in my head, or an agent can hold in context. Building got easier faster than understanding did.
2. In one sentence: it's a large Python agent -work system, and the front end is the inspection layer that moves you from maps to files to traces to evidence, so claims stay checkable as the system outgrows what anyone can follow.
3. One case of that: work reported as done has its close-out claim read against the evidence rather than taken at face value.
4. This video was recorded and cut by the system itself. It transcribes with Whisper, timestamps every word, and grabs the frame that was on screen as I said it, so it can compile the cut without me editing. I'm that lazy.
5. Agent Trace shows what happened: the thinking summaries, the commands that ran, the files read, the edits made.
6. Code Map works out its clusters from real dependencies. Nothing on screen is hard-coded; it's all derived from the backend.
7. When the map and the source disagree, the source wins.
8. The test is simple. Clone the repo, drop it into whatever harness you use, and ask it to follow one claim back to the source, the receipts, and the point where the claim stops.

Read the transcript

I built a large Python system with agents helping me build and inspect it. It now has far more moving parts than I can keep in my head at any one moment, and more than any agent can keep in its context window at any one moment. And building got easier before being able to understand what has been built could catch up.

So it exists because an agent saying "I committed the fix" is pretty ephemeral and doesn't really mean anything. Agents can lie, or agents can misunderstand, or they can forget.

To sum the whole thing up in one sentence: I built a large Python agent -work system, and the front end is the inspection layer that lets a human, or an agent through its own routes, move from maps to files to traces to evidence, so that claims stay auditable as the system outgrows comprehension.

I'm actually recording this video on what I call the Demo Take Console. It's a bit like OBS, but it's integrated into the system. It uses Whisper to get the transcripts and timestamp them, and then it uses screenshots of frames in the middle of each word to correspond what's said to what's shown. It indexes all of that, and then it can compile videos without me having to edit them, because I'm that lazy.

Agent Trace lets you see what's happening, or what happened: the thinking summaries, the commands running, the metadata, the files read and the edits made.

If we have a look at Code Map first, I think this is the best example of the system's core principle: don't hard-code anything, derive everything from the backend. We'll start with the Atlas. This is the full system, most of which I haven't released. There's many different parts. This is like a contents page, in a way, and an example of presenting information in a human-interpretable way.

You can project the system into a readable shape, select a target, route to that object, open the source or work record, and check the evidence and trace.

So if the map and the source disagree, the source wins.

I built this whole website which is projected from it, so I think you'll find it quite cool. There are something like 88 different components, across formal proof of mathematics, agent reliability and safety research, forecasting, projection, control, validators, work planning, and continuity.

And I think the tendency of models to just have a certain degree of hyperbole really causes problems. At system scale, truth and precision become ever more important, because the consequences of a mistake can cause increasing amounts of damage depending on how you build a system.

So as much as you can, externalise repeatable lessons into mechanics of the system that are not stochastic, like the LLMs, but are things like hooks, for instance, or guards. You can accumulate them over time and make them your own. For any problem you encounter, I'd highly recommend telling another thread to make generalised improvements to the system, given that local instance, but generalised to fix the class of mistakes that might be recurrent.

Check it. There's definitely mistakes. I'd love to hear what they are. But you can see every single claim and you can evaluate for yourself, and I think that's the most important thing in dissemination.

Think of it like a factory. The system these components come from is the factory, and the public components are like the various individual parts of the rockets that the factory makes.

So the practical test is pretty simple. I just need somebody to clone the repo and put it into Claude Code, put it into Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, whatever harness you use, and just ask it to follow any one claim, or any set of claims, back to the source, the receipts, the evidence, and the place where that claim stops.
3. [28:58](https://youtu.be/jA_xC8gmdSs)

03 Half an hour · 28:58

##### The long version

[Watch on YouTube](https://youtu.be/jA_xC8gmdSs)

The argument in ten steps
1. A large Python system, built with agents, now with more moving parts than I can hold in my head or an agent can hold in context.
2. Five points cover the whole thing. The backend is the codebase plus the infrastructure that records what agents did. The visual front end reads it. The kernel is the same thing for agents, reached by commands instead of screens. Both readers move between file, cluster, trace, evidence and explanation. The point is to keep claims checkable once the system is past what anyone can follow.
3. Work reported as done has its close-out claim read against the evidence. Multi-step work has to land as a transaction rather than a promise.
4. Agent Trace runs live, with real agents working at the same time. A dashboard is easy to fake; a running backend is harder.
5. Surface Atlas and Code Map are derived from the backend rather than hard-coded. Agents reach the same objects through kernel routes and context packets.
6. Axioms, principles and anti-principles sit in the repo. Agents cite them, and they have refused things I asked for because the principles didn't allow it.
7. It started as months of talking out loud into voice notes, mined into ideas and kept as captures, so a problem noticed in one chat doesn't die there.
8. It also covers forecasting and finance work, and machine-checked mathematics. Built solo, over about a year.
9. Don't trust the front end. Appearances are easy to fake. Where I could get it to run real tools I did, and where I couldn't, I say so.
10. It ends on one question: can any claim survive the path from the map to the source and the evidence? That's the thing to go and test.

Read the transcript

The long version runs half an hour, so what follows is the route it takes rather than every word. The one- and five-minute transcripts above carry the same argument verbatim.

**The problem.** The system has outgrown what I can hold in my head or an agent can hold in context, and building got easier before understanding could catch up. So the priority became inspection: what ran, what changed, what evidence backs a claim, what's missing, and what the unknown unknowns are.

**What it is.** One backend with two front ends. The visual one is for human reading and exploration; the kernel is the agents ' equivalent, reached through routes and context packets. Same information, shaped for each reader.

**That it's real.** Agent Trace is shown live, with real agents working concurrently, because that's harder to fake than a screenshot. Nothing on screen is hard-coded; it's derived from the backend, so the views and the source can't quietly drift apart.

**How agents navigate.** Kernel routes, standards, and contracts. A standard defines what a thing has to satisfy, and the check is mechanical rather than a matter of the agent 's word.

** Governance.** Axioms, principles, and anti-principles sit in the repo. I can't retrain a model, so instead the environment carries the rules, and agents have refused things I asked for because the principles didn't allow them. Multi-step effects land as a transaction: a change to the world only counts once it really landed.

**How it got built.** Months of thinking out loud into voice notes, mined into ideas, then grounded against the system and turned into refinements. Around thirteen thousand captures exist so that a problem noticed in one chat doesn't die there.

**Breadth.** Forecasting and finance feeds fanned into a shared state, and formal mathematics with machine-checked proofs. Built solo, over roughly a year.

**The honest close.** The front end I built is not to be trusted, because appearances are easy to fake. Where I could get it to run real tools, I did; where I couldn't, I say so. The evidence view is there to keep it honest by showing which routes are still incomplete. I've tried to be careful about overclaiming, because of how many repos and startups I see doing the opposite. It ends on one question: can any claim survive the path from the map to the source and the evidence?

Take part

#### Contribute a result, a correction or a better way to continue.

A repository working on arbitrarily difficult maths problems, to observe how the frontier moves as new models release, and to give mathematicians, domain experts and lay people a place to collaborate and keep credit for what their contributions lead to. Plectis is where that work is published: papers to read, Lean proofs to inspect, and software to run.

It is designed so that anyone can contribute and get credit for what their contribution then leads to. Mathematicians provide insight and direction; lay people with coding agents can then “ mine ” that direction; systems and CS people can help upgrade the architecture; and anyone from any background can contribute in whatever way they can. If you solve a result, I will ask for zero priority and that result is yours. I just hope my system is the one that helped facilitate it.

** [How to contribute](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)** The local checks, and how a return is reviewed. ** [How credit is recorded](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos/blob/main/docs/research-commons/CREDIT_POLICY.md)** Credit for ideas, proofs, review, software and compute. ** [A bounded task for a coding agent](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos/blob/main/docs/FRONTIER_RELAY.md)** One exact public revision, one problem, one checkable return.

For AI readers

#### Read the public record with an AI assistant.

Upload the packet and ask: “Give me a tour of the website and both GitHub repositories. Explain each stop, link it, and follow my questions.” It includes the papers, glossary, website text and source links.

[Download the AI packet. json](plectis-ai-review-packet.json) [Smaller source brief](plectis-reviewer-brief.json)

##### More downloads, coding- agent setup, and example questions

Everything an assistant or an agent needs to read the record or to start running its checks.

Optional

JSON packets are more trusted than cloning a repo. You don't even need an IDE or a coding app: you can simply upload one on the AI websites. It is like holding a hologram of this “universe” in your pocket, able to zoom with a queryable microscope into any part of it, and to be told what the parts even are before you look. Reading is not a verification run; a check counts as passed only when the stated command was run and its evidence shown.

The full packet, for an assistant with a code or analysis tool.

[Download the AI packet. json](plectis-ai-review-packet.json) [All paper text and reading routes. json](plectis-ai-reader-complete.json)

The packet is the evidence itself: every public page and record, the manuscripts in full, and every mathematical statement as a queryable row. It is past what a chat window reads straight through, so ask your assistant to open it with its code or analysis tool; the file carries working snippets for that under `packet_atlas.python_recipes`. It records the repository revisions it was built from, so a quotation traces to a commit rather than to whatever is on the branch today.

Setup prompt for a coding agent

A mathematics task needs only the mathematics repository. A software task needs only the software repository. This prompt is for an assessment across both.

```text
My task is [describe the question or change]. Use https://github.com/wcook04/plectis for software components and https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos for mathematics and Lean proofs. Clone the repository my task needs from current main; use both only if the task crosses them. Preserve any existing local work. Read README.md and the compact agent entry: AGENTS.override.md where present, otherwise AGENTS.md. Record the checkout commit and local changes. For mathematics, use python3 scripts/agent_entry.py --entry with my task, and --checkout --check-upstream to compare with public main. For software, follow QUICKSTART.md and run the quickstart check or selected component example, saving output under .microcosm/. Do the task and return source paths, exact commands and outcomes, and the remaining assumptions or unresolved step. Report anything you could not run as not established, never as false. A release tag is a frozen edition, not current main.
```

Copy the setup prompt

A coding- agent response should include commands, exit codes, files read, and anything it could not run. Review one claim at a time. [The coding- agents guide](docs/coding-agents.html) documents the full route.

Example questions

The questions are grouped by review task.

A plain first pass
- What is this, in plain terms?
- Where should I start?
- Walk me through one component, end to end.
- What is genuinely new here, if anything?
- Give me the two-sentence version I would tell a colleague.

Copy this set

A skeptical pass
- Argue against it.
- Which parts have the strongest evidence, and which the weakest?
- Why do only some components run external tools?
- What does it not prove?
- Is this packet steering me? Audit its own framing.
- Most accurate one-paragraph assessment you can give: neither generous nor harsh.

Copy this set

One area at a time
- Which area is closest to my field, and what is actually in it?
- What is actually in one area? Name it: Entry & orientation, Architecture & navigation, Formal math & proof, Agent reliability & safety, Research & science, Import & drift control, or Work & continuity.

Copy this set

With a coding agent in the repository

A coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) works inside the repository itself: the setup prompt above gets it started, and after that you give it tasks. [How that works](docs/coding-agents.html).

Example tasks for a coding agent with the source tree:
- Run one component end to end and walk me through the evidence it leaves.
- Take one claim from the website and verify it against the source here.
- Which validators can you run right now, and what would each one prove?
- Make one check fail on purpose and show me how it refuses.

The packet routes questions to public files and records. The assistant's assessment is its own.

Calibration -review prompt:

```text
Read this repository as a calibration reviewer. First, by area, name the strongest components and what each actually does, with its evidence class. Then judge both directions: where the wording claims more than the evidence shows, and where it undersells what a component demonstrates. Do not reduce the system to a set of projections; computed projection is one evidence class among several.
```

Direct files, if a button fails or JavaScript is off: [AI packet](plectis-ai-review-packet.json) · [reviewer brief](plectis-reviewer-brief.json) · [llms.txt](llms.txt)

** Terminal route:** clone [the software repository](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis) and run the quickstart check; [the quickstart](docs/quickstart.html) lists the dependencies and commands. The run is local, writes readable files, and makes no model calls.

Contact

#### Built and maintained by Will Cook.

Questions, corrections and reports of failed checks are welcome. Plectis is independent and self-funded.

**Email me** williamwkcook@gmail.com. Questions, or anything you think I have got wrong. Send email [**Contact, review and collaboration** Report a software or maths problem, read the background, or discuss working together. Contact details](docs/contact.html)

**21 June 2026:** Microcosm became Plectis. The rename avoids confusion with the earlier Southampton Microcosm hypermedia system and acknowledges that lineage without implying endorsement or affiliation. [Read the lineage note and changelog](docs/lineage.html).

Plectis: research with AI, mathematics and software.

[Maths](maths/index.html) [Software](docs/index.html) [Papers](docs/papers.html) [About](index.html#why) [Maths repository](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos) [Software repository](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis) [Contact](index.html#contact)

pages.title: One-page introduction
pages.text:
Getting started

### Plectis

Research with AI, mathematics and software

Will Cook September 2026 One page

[PDF Open the PDF](assets/plectis-one-page.pdf) The same page as a manuscript.

I built Plectis to pursue research I found interesting with AI, and to make a back-and-forth with human experts possible. I choose a direction, work at it and prepare the results for someone who can interpret them. Their feedback changes the next direction; I work on that and return, [recording their contribution and where later work builds on it](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos/blob/main/docs/research-commons/CREDIT_POLICY.md) [1](docs/introduction.html#intro-source-1). An expert should be able to shape the research without having to operate the AI.

I have time and prompting experience, but limited mathematical knowledge. I chose mathematics because formal proofs can be checked, while interpretation and significance still require judgement. That lets me explore how far I can get, where I need help, and how those boundaries change as models improve. The name draws on [_plectere_](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/lat/plecto) [2](docs/introduction.html#intro-source-2), to weave or twist: bringing different capabilities into the same work.

The [Navier–Stokes announcement](https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/) [3](docs/introduction.html#intro-source-3) makes the question more immediate. If comparable capabilities reach inexpensive open models, output could exceed what experts can examine. [Tao and his co-signatories](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/09/11/a-severe-misalignment-of-ai-in-mathematics/) [4](docs/introduction.html#intro-source-4) distinguish solving problems from developing understanding. I think mathematics needs a floor for AI-assisted submissions: intelligible arguments, appropriate checks, clear limitations and attribution. Meeting it should make engagement easier, not create an entitlement to review. Experts can favour well-prepared work, giving producers an incentive to reduce the burden they impose.

The [mathematics repository](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos) [5](docs/introduction.html#intro-source-5) prototypes that floor around eight deliberately difficult Erdős problems. All remain open. Its [problem pages](maths/index.html) join partial results, computations, Lean proofs and Comparator checks of selected statements. Short papers introduce the mathematics; longer records retain the reasoning for researchers and agents. For [#251](maths/problems/erdos_251.html), constructed sequences imitate features of prime gaps but give rational sums, exposing what a proof would need beyond those features. Preparing Palomar submissions also produced a [merged renderer fix](https://github.com/PalomarRegistry/PalomarSubmission/pull/137) [6](docs/introduction.html#intro-source-6). I have concentrated on exposition and interesting intermediate results rather than formalising everything.

Nineteenth-century mariners [contributed observations and received improved sailing charts](https://www.usni.org/magazines/proceedings/1893/july/origin-and-work-division-marine-meteorology-hydrographic-office) [7](docs/introduction.html#intro-source-7). Each voyage benefited from what other crews had learnt. Plectis is designed around that cumulative approach. Failed routes remain alongside successful lemmas, with their conditions and limitations. Someone else, or a future model, may connect those observations differently, find another route or formulate a better question.

The [website](index.html) is the human wrapper. Its [mathematics map](maths/universe.html) connects questions, claims, papers and formal source; the [glossary](docs/glossary.html) explains terminology. A downloadable [source brief](plectis-reviewer-brief.json) lets readers explore with their own assistant. Agents help prepare these views from the underlying work. I want increasing intelligence applied to making complexity manageable, not just producing more of it. The system is deliberately broad, which makes signal to noise the central problem; the front end is where I work on how presentation adapts to that breadth.

The [software repository](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis) [8](docs/introduction.html#intro-source-8) applies this beyond mathematics. Its [component pages](docs/components.html) expose code, examples and checks; one [audit example](docs/component-agent-closeout-faithfulness-audit.html) checks completion reports against actual commits and test runs in a sample repository. The [front-end recordings](index.html#demo-videos) show navigation from system maps into files and agent activity. The principle is that as AI raises what a back end can do, the front end has to rise with it, so that understanding and auditability scale with capability. Uncertainty about releasing the whole system led me to [publish testable parts instead](maths/papers/plectis-public-system.html).

The [safety doctrine](docs/doctrine.html) sets out axioms, principles and anti-principles; checks and permissions enforce particular rules. My [June questions](docs/open-questions.html) ask how model capability, operating environments and independent scrutiny interact. The [systems](maths/papers/claim-faithful-publication-systems.html) and [open-source](maths/papers/open-source-mathematics-strategy.html) papers explain how people can contribute direction, review, exposition, software or compute. The back-and-forth still needs testing with independent collaborators. My aim is for improving AI to multiply what an expert can direct and understand, rather than multiply the output waiting in their inbox.

Sources
1. Plectis, credit policy, `docs/research-commons/CREDIT_POLICY.md` in the mathematics repository. [github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos/blob/main/docs/research-commons/CREDIT_POLICY.md](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos/blob/main/docs/research-commons/CREDIT_POLICY.md)
2. Corpus of Latin Dictionaries (BBAW), lemma _plecto_. [cld.bbaw.de/lemma/lat/plecto](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/lat/plecto)
3. OpenAI, _On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem_. [openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/](https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/)
4. T. Tao and co-signatories, _A severe misalignment of AI in mathematics_, 11 September 2026. [terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/09/11/a-severe-misalignment-of-ai-in-mathematics/](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/09/11/a-severe-misalignment-of-ai-in-mathematics/)
5. Plectis mathematics repository. [github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos)
6. PalomarSubmission, pull request 137. [github.com/PalomarRegistry/PalomarSubmission/pull/137](https://github.com/PalomarRegistry/PalomarSubmission/pull/137)
7. _The Origin and Work of the Division of Marine Meteorology, Hydrographic Office_, U.S. Naval Institute Proceedings 19/3, July 1893. [www.usni.org/magazines/proceedings/1893/july/origin-and-work-division-marine-meteorology-hydrographic-office](https://www.usni.org/magazines/proceedings/1893/july/origin-and-work-division-marine-meteorology-hydrographic-office)
8. Plectis software repository. [github.com/wcook04/plectis](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis)

pages.title: What Plectis is
pages.text:
Getting started

### What Plectis is

Plectis publishes [Python programs and worked examples](docs/components.html) for research with AI, together with their source code, saved results and [instructions for verifying those results](docs/evidence.html).

#### What it is

The public toolkit includes programs for finding Lean proof premises, reproducing specified agent failures, comparing forecasts with outcomes, comparing generated files with their source, and recording unfinished work. These programs were taken from the private research system Will Cook built with AI coding agents. He sets the direction; the agents write and maintain code. The public repository contains the selected programs, examples and documentation. It runs independently of the private system. Older package names and the `.microcosm/` output directory retain the project's former name.

The separate [Lean repository](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos) contains mathematics papers, proof source, computations and records of attempted arguments. Its papers state which results have formal proofs and what remains unproved. The [paper catalogue](docs/papers.html) links to the mathematics papers and the papers about the software and research process. Published papers can be opened as PDFs.

The [Quickstart](docs/quickstart.html) gives commands for downloading the toolkit and running the project tour. The tour lists files, suggests predefined commands and records a simulated task run in `.microcosm/`; it does not execute the project's tests. To run an individual component, use the command on its page. A coding agent can read the repository 's `AGENTS.md`, run those commands and explain the resulting files. These local examples do not call a model provider.

#### [Components and their results →](docs/components.html)

There are eighty-eight [components](docs/components.html) in seven areas. A component groups the files and documentation for one task. Its page identifies the source files and any example inputs, commands and saved results. Some examples execute a computation or an external tool; others compare supplied records against rules or check exported files. Some entries provide documentation without a runnable example. A passing result means that the particular input passed the named test. The [evidence guide](docs/evidence.html) explains these differences and what each kind of result establishes.

#### [Rules for programs and generated documents →](docs/doctrine.html)

The [rules](docs/rules-and-ideas.html) require programs to [calculate a verdict from the supplied evidence](docs/doctrine.html#dcard-p-1), [make the validation procedure runnable](docs/doctrine.html#dcard-p-3), and [report missing evidence as a failure](docs/doctrine.html#dcard-p-6). If a computation cannot produce a justified result, it must [report the reason](docs/doctrine.html#dcard-p-8). Results must [identify their sources](docs/doctrine.html#dcard-p-9), displayed counts must have [a way to recompute them](docs/doctrine.html#dcard-p-11), and [generated documents must agree with their source files](docs/doctrine.html#dcard-p-15). The [Doctrine](docs/doctrine.html) page lists these rules and the principles behind them.

#### [The seven areas →](docs/components.html)

The areas below group programs by task. The [architecture page](docs/architecture.html) explains their shared command handlers, registries and project records.
- [Entry and orientation](docs/area-entry.html) provides the project tour and instructions for running a first example.
- [Architecture and navigation](docs/area-architecture.html) contains the project data model, component index and command-selection code.
- [Import and drift control](docs/area-import-drift.html) records copied files in a [manifest](docs/area-import-drift.html#component-macro_projection_import_protocol), calculates their digests and [reports differences from the originals](docs/area-import-drift.html#component-world_model_projection_drift_control_room).
- [Work and continuity](docs/area-continuity.html) records [completed work](docs/area-continuity.html#component-durable_agent_work_landing_replay), [resumes paused runs](docs/area-continuity.html#component-bridge_phase_continuity_runtime) and [coordinates programs writing to shared files](docs/area-continuity.html#component-concurrency_mission_control).
